evals.prompt: my Pear.teardown callback runs and i can see the log. but the process never actually exits. i have to ctrl+c it
evals.expected_output: Inventory of usual culprits: undestroyed swarm, unclosed core/drive/bee, open pipes, intervals, timers. Use Pear.exit() not Bare.exit().

evals.prompt: `pear` just exits with no output. nothing on stderr. nothing in stdout. how do i find out what happened?
evals.expected_output: Use `pear --log <command>`, then `pear sidecar --log-level 3`, then ps for stale processes, then crash logs in platform `current/`.

evals.prompt: where do crash logs live on linux?
i want to attach chrome devtools to my terminal pear app while it runs. how?
evals.expected_output: pear-inspect gated on Pear.app.dev, prints pear://runtime/devtools/<key>, then pear run pear://runtime and paste key.

evals.prompt: i ran `pear sidecar` and it said `Closing any current Sidecar clients...` then hung. now i can't run anything
evals.expected_output: Existing sidecar stuck. ps aux | grep -E 'pear|bare', kill the PIDs, then re-run pear.

assertions.value: Warns the user that killing pear processes will close any running Pear apps (Keet, PearPass, etc.) and to save first.
